name: Block print on fabric
blurb: Carve a stamp, print a repeat, and plain fabric becomes your own design. Fast results, and the carving skill transfers straight to lino printing on paper.
gear: Soft carving blocks and lino tools
Fabric printing ink and a brayer
Cotton fabric and a padded printing surface
steps: Design something simple with bold shapes. Fine detail is fragile and prints badly on fabric.
Transfer the design in reverse and carve away everything you do not want printed, cutting away from your hands.
Test print on paper and refine the carving.
Roll a thin, even layer of ink onto the block — too much ink fills the detail and blurs.
Print with firm even pressure onto fabric backed by a padded surface, and learn to register a repeat.
Heat set the ink with an iron so it survives washing.
tips: Always carve away from your other hand and use a bench hook. Lino tools slip and cut deeply.
Unset ink washes straight out. Heat setting is what makes it permanent.
proof: A printed length of fabric with a clean repeat that survives a wash.
